hazard_description: Adding water to concentrated sulfuric acid causes instantaneous localized boiling and violent acid splattering (-Delta H). Always add acid to water slowly with stirring.
warning_speech: Danger! Never pour water directly into concentrated sulfuric acid. It produces extreme exothermic heat and violent acid splattering. Always add acid slowly to water.

hazard_description: Adding water directly to concentrated hydrochloric acid releases corrosive hydrogen chloride gas and heat. Always add acid slowly to water in a fume hood.
warning_speech: Caution! Always add hydrochloric acid to water, never water to acid, to prevent rapid heating and corrosive vapor release.
lcd_message:
CAUTION: ACID DILUTION
ADD ACID TO WATER

hazard_description: Mixing bleach with ammonia forms toxic and potentially explosive chloramine gases (NH2Cl, NHCl2, NCl3), causing severe respiratory trauma and pulmonary edema.
warning_speech: Critical safety hazard! Never mix bleach with ammonia. This reaction generates lethal chloramine gases. Evacuate immediately if fumes are detected.

hazard_description: Bleach reacts with acids to produce toxic chlorine gas (Cl2). Inhaling chlorine gas causes violent coughing, chemical burns to respiratory membranes, and asphyxiation.
warning_speech: Danger! Mixing bleach with acid liberates deadly chlorine gas. Do not combine these reagents. Use a certified chemical fume hood.

hazard_description: Cyanide salts combined with acids immediately release highly lethal hydrogen cyanide gas (HCN), inhibiting cellular respiration within seconds.
warning_speech: Fatal hazard alert! Cyanide salts combined with acid produce deadly hydrogen cyanide gas. Never mix cyanides with acidic solutions.

hazard_description: Nitric acid is a potent oxidizer that reacts violently with organic solvents, resulting in spontaneous ignition, rapid overpressure, and toxic nitrogen dioxide fumes.
warning_speech: Severe explosion risk! Nitric acid reacts violently with organic solvents. Do not mix nitric acid with alcohols or ketones.

hazard_description: KMnO4 reacts with glycerol in an intensely exothermic autoignition reaction, producing high heat and open flames after a short induction delay.
warning_speech: Warning! Potassium permanganate with glycerol produces spontaneous combustion and severe thermal fire. Keep strictly separated.

hazard_description: Concentrated peroxide undergoes rapid catalytic decomposition when exposed to transition metals (Fe2+, MnO2), causing vigorous boiling and aerosol ejection.
warning_speech: Caution! Transition metal catalysts cause rapid peroxide decomposition, gas pressure spikes, and chemical boilover.

hazard_description: Alkali metals react violently with water, releasing flammable hydrogen gas and immense heat which ignites the hydrogen explosively.
warning_speech: Critical hazard! Sodium and potassium react explosively with water, releasing self-igniting hydrogen gas. Store under mineral oil only.

hazard_description: Prolonged standing or drying of ammoniacal silver solutions forms highly shock-sensitive silver nitride (fulminating silver) which detonates on touch.
warning_speech: Caution! Ammoniacal silver solutions must be neutralized immediately after use to prevent explosive silver fulminate accumulation.
